text:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Dedicated pool dp-23 error rate spike >10% over 5m (region: us-west1). Paging oncall.
alex: got the page, pulling metrics now. seeing 500s from model shard nodes during token generation.
maria: I'm in. any customer-facing errors reported yet?
alex: one support ticket from AcmeCorp reporting timeouts on /v1/generate, sample error: "upstream reset by peer". traffic to dp-23 has a sharp surge — looks like a promo spike.
samir: copying perf dashboard: 95th latency 2.8s -> 6.5s, gpu_util near 98% on some hosts.
tara: can we enable burst capacity for dp-23? this pool is Dedicated and has burst toggle available.
alex: agree. Quick mitigation plan: 1) enable burst capacity x2 for dp-23 for 30m 2) reduce per-tenant concurrency for noisy tenants 3) enable rate-limit for anonymous/low-tier traffic 4) if needed, disable experimental streaming transform feature that's increasing token work.
adeem: typo — it's Nadeem not adeem :grin:
adeem: on it. I'll flip burst and add a temporary quota for the top noisy tenants. executing command now:
```
# enable burst capacity 2x for 30m
redwoodctl pools update --pool dp-23 --burst-multiplier 2.0 --burst-duration 30m
```
deploy-bot: job queued: redwoodctl pools update (id: job-8721). rolling update in progress.
alex: while burst spins up, can we apply per-key rate-limit for public API keys? maybe set qps=5 for free tier.
maria: creating a quick policy change via admin API:
```
POST /admin/v1/quotas
{
  "policy": "temporary_tier_rate_limit",
  "targets": ["free-tier","anon"],
  "qps": 5,
  "duration": "30m"
}
```
ops-sre: applied temporary policy, confirmed 200. logs show 429s increase for anon but overall load dropped ~18%.
samir: burst toggle completed. GPU utilization dropped from 98% -> 72% on overloaded hosts. latency recovering.
tara: nice. any customers still impacted?
alex: AcmeCorp still seeing occasional 502s but tracing shows requests routed to fallback model variant (lower-capacity) for some tokens.
maria: I've pushed a rollback for the streaming-transform feature flag for dp-23 to reduce CPU overhead:
```
flags set dp-23 streaming-transform=false --scope=dedicated
```
nadeem: flag change acknowledged. deploy-bot: flag rollout succeeded on dp-23.
alex: request rate is stabilizing. I'm keeping burst for full 30m and will re-evaluate at +20m.
IncidentBot: Incident severity set to S2 (customer impact limited, mitigation in place). Incident owner: alex.
tara: heads-up: autoscaler logs show we hit max-scale for dp-23; consider increasing max if promo continues — but that requires quota approval for Dedicated.
samir: as a stopgap we can increase burst to 3x for another 15m if traffic persists, but need approval from infra lead for >2x sustained.
maria: I'll notify sales/CS for AcmeCorp and open a support short report. Posting brief to #customer-impact.
alex: handing off to tara for the night. summary: burst enabled 2x for 30m, free-tier qps=5, streaming-transform disabled on dp-23, monitoring in place. watchlist on latency and 5xx.
 tara: taking over. I'll keep the chat pinned and will escalate if error rate >5% again. ping me @tara if anything changes.
IncidentBot: On-call handover logged: from alex to tara at 2475002420.
alex: quick note — we also adjusted canary routing: fallback to smaller model variants when queue depth > 200 to preserve throughput.
ops-sre: added a temporary quota bump for enterprise customers impacted (AcmeCorp + 2 others) to reduce throttling while we stabilize.
alex: good. after stabilization, we should schedule an RCA — potential causes: promotional surge, autoscale thresholds too conservative, streaming-transform CPU overhead.
tara: ack. I'll open the incident ticket and assign RCA to samir + infra. tagging for follow-up: @infra-lead @perf-eng.
IncidentBot: incident closed for paging purposes at 2475003480. resolution: mitigations applied, customers stable. Postmortem required: yes (owner: samir). :white_check_mark:
